headline: Monitor Volcanic Activity and Backcountry Permits
reservation: Standard entry requires a park pass; however, all backcountry camping requires a specific permit through the official NPS system. Volcanic conditions change rapidly, potentially closing areas; check the official USGS and NPS alerts daily before heading to the summit.

days.title: The Smoking Summit

stops.name: Kilauea Overlook
stops.detail: Observe the massive scale of the caldera from the rim; visibility is typically highest in the early morning.

stops.name: Nahuku (Thurston Lava Tube)
stops.detail: Walk through a massive underground passage formed by ancient lava flows, surrounded by lush fern forest.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for summit area travel; conditions vary
days.note: High altitude and sulfur gases can affect breathing; stay on marked paths to avoid steam vents.

days.title: Lava Lake Descent
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from the Kilauea Iki Trailhead

stops.name: Kilauea Iki Trail
stops.detail: Hike down through rainforest onto the solidified floor of a former lava lake, a landscape of cracked basalt.

stops.name: Pu‘upua‘i Overlook
stops.detail: View the cinder cone formed during the 1959 eruption and see the contrast of regenerating life.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for trailhead access; conditions vary
days.note: Lava rock is abrasive and holds heat; sturdy footwear and sun protection are essential for the crater floor.

days.title: The Coastal Descent
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Chain of Craters Road
stops.detail: Drive the scenic 19-mile route that drops 3,700 feet to the sea, passing numerous historic lava flows.

stops.name: Hōlei Sea Arch
stops.detail: Witness the power of the Pacific at this dramatic basalt arch located at the road's end.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for the round trip drive and stops; conditions vary
days.note: There is no fuel or food along this road; ensure your tank is full before leaving the summit.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Parking at Kilauea Iki and Nahuku often fills by mid-morning during peak seasons. Use the early morning hours for these popular spots to ensure access.

intel.title: Summit Only
intel.text: While the visitor center has basic coverage, signal drops entirely as you descend Chain of Craters Road. Do not rely on streaming GPS for the coastal section.

intel.title: Village Supplies
intel.text: Volcano Village is the last reliable stop for fuel and groceries before entering the park. Hilo offers more expansive options for those arriving from the airport.

intel.title: Elevation Weather
intel.text: The summit is often 15 degrees cooler than the coast and frequently wet. Suggested hiking times prioritize early starts to beat the midday tropical heat.

intel.title: Lava Stability
intel.text: Coastal cliffs and lava benches are inherently unstable and subject to collapse. Always respect official barriers and never enter closed zones for photography.

plan.arrival: Land at Hilo (ITO), pick up your rental car, and shop for supplies in town before the 45-minute drive to the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for paved roads; check rental contracts regarding restrictions for off-road or unpaved tracks.
plan.goldenHour: The Kilauea rim offers dramatic lighting at sunset, though cloud cover is frequent; check the Kilauea webcam for current visibility.
